summary: Mount Burke summit cabin built in 1929 (a 1937 article says the cabin dates to 1930), closed in 1953; it still stands empty, reached by a 12.5 km round-trip hike in Kananaskis Country.

facts.design: Wooden cabin with shuttered windows along its west, south and east walls, guyed with cables to the treeline

access.note: Hike to the summit in Kananaskis Country; no closure or permit described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Start at the parking area; the old approach began at the lot outside Cataract Creek campground, and a cutline now replaces it after the 2013 floods. The 2020 round trip was 12.5 km, about four hours up and three down; the trail is well marked.

events.note: Alberta Historic Places, DanOCan 2025 and Canada Lookouts (citing a 1998 book) give 1929 for the first lookout structure. A 1937 Calgary Herald article quoted by DanOCan 2020 and Canada Lookouts says the cabin was built in 1930; see resolved_conflicts.
Registered June 5, 1996; nominated by Bob Young, Alberta Land and Forest Service
Closed in favor of two lower sites, Raspberry Ridge and Hailstone Butte. A 2020 blog gave 1954 from another blog; the author found no firsthand source for 1954.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Canada Lookouts dates the first lookout structure to 1929, and the 1937 Calgary Herald says the cabin was built in 1930. The sources read do not say whether the 1929 structure was the same cabin.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the register says the Canadian Forest Service built it; DanOCan 2025 says the Alberta Forest Service. Unresolved: elevation (register 2,504 m; Alberta Historic Places 2,540 m; 1930 Herald 2,542 m). Unresolved: closing year 1953 (Alberta Historic Places, DanOCan 2025, Canada Lookouts) vs 1954 (a 2020 blog quoting another blog, unconfirmed). The record's name Cameron Lookout is kept; Alberta Historic Places says it was first called Burke Lookout. The register's 1996 maintenance plan was not followed up in any source read. Not used: Grokipedia, YouTube result snippets and a reader comment on DanOCan, which were leads only. No local_unit is in the brief, so none is written. Brief status 'standing' is supported by the 2025 visit. No photos added. Used 2 WebSearch-equivalent queries and 6 page reads.
